newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu battles crises in peace and politics.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu battles crises in peace and politics.

text.p: Israeli troops battled Palestinian protesters on the streets of Hebron while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fought a cabinet crisis overshadowing any Middle East peace moves.

Troops firing rubber bullets shot and wounded 14 people -- including a boy seriously injured in the head -- during protests by Palestinians who hurled firebombs and stones at the soldiers in the flashpoint West Bank town.
"The government is not ready to accept a norm of street violence simultaneous to political negotiations," a statement quoted Netanyahu as telling his cabinet.
"We conveyed very sharp messages to the Palestinians on this matter...We must wait and see whether these messages will be answered," he said.
Hebron has been ravaged by violence since a Jewish woman angered Arabs last week by putting up anti-Moslem posters depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
A home-made bomb exploded in an alley in Hebron's casbah but caused no injuries.
"Whoever throws a bomb with the intention of killing someone will also meet his death," Major-General Gabi Ofir, Israel's West Bank commander, told Israeli army radio.

In Jerusalem, Netanyahu sought to defuse the latest in a series of crises -- this one with Foreign Minister David Levy -- which have plagued his government since he came to power nearly 13 months ago.
Levy, 59, fears his status as formal coordinator of peace talks policy could be eroded by the expected ascent of hawkish ex-general Ariel Sharon, 69, to the vacant post of finance minister.

Asked if the problem was that he reported to Netanyahu, 47, while the Israeli leader merely spat in his face, Levy told the daily Maariv: "To my great regret that's the situation. And thus it cannot go on any longer."

Sources close to the Israeli leader said Netanyahu's foreign policymaker Uzi Arad had put off a planned trip to London and Washington until next week so as not to give rise to any further charges by Levy of a failure to coordinate.
Levy has promised an answer soon on whether he will stay in the government. A loss of Levy's support would leave Netanyahu with the barest of parliamentary majorities, possibly forcing new elections.

Israel's ally Washington said both sides were equally responsible for violence in Hebron, where 400 Jews live among 100,000 Arabs. The State Department condemned the pig posters, calling the 26-year woman who posted them "either sick or evil."

Israeli leaders have condemned the poster. Tatyans Suskin has been charged with illegally posting the placards and with endangering life by stoning an Arab car -- offences that together carry a maximum 24-year sentence.
Israel has warned Palestinians of a stronger military response unless they put an end to the violence.
Arafat's aide Nabil Abu Rdainah said Netanyahu had "provoked the Palestinian masses by assaulting their rights, stealing land, and widening settlements".
Israeli-PLO talks collapsed in March, after Netanyahu's government enraged Arabs by breaking ground on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
In Geneva, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan told Maariv he was saddened by the bloodshed and the crisis in peacemaking.
"I hope very much the peace process will be implemented and we won't arrive at a need for sanctions," he said.
